chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who stole an item, but he denied it (argued against the claim). So he was whipped. Then he produced it (the stolen item) exactly. Would the cutting be obligated upon him? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes. But, had he acknowledged (the theft) and did not produce the stolen item, his hand would not be cut, because he acknowledged (the theft) while bearing the punishment (of whipping).

key_terms.الْعَذَاب: Punishment (specifically referring to the whipping in this context)
key_terms.كَابَرَ: To deny or argue against a claim

ai.seo_question: Does producing the stolen item after being whipped for denial affect the obligation of cutting the hand in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the conditions for hadd punishment in theft, emphasizing that the production of the stolen goods (bayyinah) is crucial for the cutting of the hand, even after initial denial and whipping. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that confession alone, without the physical evidence of the stolen item, exempts the thief from the hadd penalty, distinguishing between the punishment for denial (whipping) and the punishment for the theft itself. This ruling underscores the importance of tangible proof in applying hadd punishments to prevent injustice.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who stole something, but he argued from it. So he was whipped. So he came with it (the stolen item) exactly. Would the cutting be Obligated upon him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. But, had he acknowledged, and did not come with the stolen item, his hand would not be cut, because he would have acknowledged (his theft) upon the punishment’.
